questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Atomic Orbital Nodes and Energy Levels
questions.question: How many radial and planar nodes are present in an unhybridized carbon 2p orbital?

options.label: A
options.text: Zero nodes of any kind.

options.label: B
options.text: Two spherical nodal surfaces.

options.label: C
options.text: Three perpendicular nodal planes.

options.label: D
options.text: One planar nodal plane passing through the nucleus and zero radial nodes.

questions.correct_answer: One planar nodal plane passing through the nucleus and zero radial nodes.
questions.explanation: A 2p atomic orbital possesses exactly one planar nodal plane passing through the nucleus where electron density is zero.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Sigma vs Pi Bonding Molecular Orbitals
questions.question: What is the orbital symmetry characteristic of a C-C σ bonding molecular orbital compared to a π orbital?

options.label: A
options.text: Both σ and π orbitals have identical symmetry.

options.label: B
options.text: The π orbital is spherically symmetric like an s orbital.

options.label: C
options.text: The σ orbital is cylindrically symmetric around the internuclear axis, whereas the π orbital has a nodal plane containing the internuclear axis.

options.label: D
options.text: The σ orbital has two perpendicular nodal planes.

questions.correct_answer: The σ orbital is cylindrically symmetric around the internuclear axis, whereas the π orbital has a nodal plane containing the internuclear axis.
questions.explanation: Sigma bonds feature cylindrical symmetry along the bond axis; pi bonds have electron density above and below a central nodal plane.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the spatial topology and nodal structure of a C-C σ* antibonding orbital?

options.label: A
options.text: It has all electron density concentrated directly between the nuclei.

options.label: B
options.text: It has zero nodes between the atoms.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a continuous torus of electron density.

options.label: D
options.text: It possesses a nodal plane perpendicular to the internuclear axis between the two carbon nuclei, with major lobes pointing outward 180° away.

questions.correct_answer: It possesses a nodal plane perpendicular to the internuclear axis between the two carbon nuclei, with major lobes pointing outward 180° away.
questions.explanation: Antibonding σ* orbitals have destructive interference between the nuclei, creating a perpendicular nodal plane and outward-directed lobes.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: sp3 vs sp2 vs sp Orbital Energy and Size
questions.question: Rank the hybrid atomic orbitals of carbon in order of increasing energy (lowest to highest):

options.label: A
options.text: sp³ < sp² < sp.

options.label: B
options.text: sp² < sp < sp³.

options.label: C
options.text: sp (50% s-character, lowest energy) < sp² (33% s-character) < sp³ (25% s-character, highest energy).

options.label: D
options.text: All carbon hybrid orbitals have identical energy.

questions.correct_answer: sp (50% s-character, lowest energy) < sp² (33% s-character) < sp³ (25% s-character, highest energy).
questions.explanation: Greater s-character places electrons closer to the positively charged nucleus, lowering the orbital potential energy.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In Frontier Molecular Orbital theory, what do the acronyms HOMO and LUMO represent?

options.label: A
options.text: Hybrid Orbital Molecular Overlap and Linear Unhybridized Molecular Orbital.

options.label: B
options.text: High Order Magnetic Orbital and Low Order Magnetic Orbital.

options.label: C
options.text: Helical Octet Molecular Octupole and Linear Unpaired Molecular Orbital.

options.label: D
options.text: Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO, the electron donor) and Lowest Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (LUMO, the electron acceptor).

questions.correct_answer: Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO, the electron donor) and Lowest Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (LUMO, the electron acceptor).
questions.explanation: The HOMO acts as the nucleophile/electron donor; the LUMO acts as the electrophile/electron acceptor in chemical reactions.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What orbital interaction forms the ground-state H₂ molecule from two hydrogen 1s atomic orbitals?

options.label: A
options.text: Out-of-phase destructive overlap yielding a σ* orbital.

options.label: B
options.text: Non-bonding electrostatic attraction without orbital mixing.

options.label: C
options.text: Sideways p-orbital overlap.

options.label: D
options.text: In-phase constructive overlap of two 1s atomic orbitals yielding a low-energy σ bonding molecular orbital with zero nodes between nuclei.

questions.correct_answer: In-phase constructive overlap of two 1s atomic orbitals yielding a low-energy σ bonding molecular orbital with zero nodes between nuclei.
questions.explanation: Constructive in-phase overlap of 1s orbitals concentrates electron density between nuclei, lowering the energy to form the σ_1s MO.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: According to Molecular Orbital theory, how are the 8 valence electrons of methane (CH₄) distributed among MOs?

options.label: A
options.text: Eight electrons in four degenerate non-bonding orbitals.

options.label: B
options.text: All 8 electrons are in eight separate, isolated single-bond orbitals.

options.label: C
options.text: Two electrons in a non-degenerate, lowest-energy a₁ MO (from C 2s) and six electrons in three degenerate t₂ MOs (from C 2p).

options.label: D
options.text: All 8 electrons in a single giant spherical orbital.

questions.correct_answer: Two electrons in a non-degenerate, lowest-energy a₁ MO (from C 2s) and six electrons in three degenerate t₂ MOs (from C 2p).
questions.explanation: Photoelectron spectroscopy confirms methane has two discrete valence ionization energies corresponding to a₁ and triply degenerate t₂ MOs.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What are the quantum characteristics of the HOMO and LUMO in neutral ethylene (H₂C=CH₂)?

options.label: A
options.text: The HOMO is ψ₂ and the LUMO is ψ₁.

options.label: B
options.text: The HOMO has two nodes and the LUMO has zero nodes.

options.label: C
options.text: The HOMO is the π bonding orbital (ψ₁, zero vertical nodes, 2 electrons); the LUMO is the π* antibonding orbital (ψ₂, one vertical node, empty).

options.label: D
options.text: Both HOMO and LUMO are completely filled with 4 electrons.

questions.correct_answer: The HOMO is the π bonding orbital (ψ₁, zero vertical nodes, 2 electrons); the LUMO is the π* antibonding orbital (ψ₂, one vertical node, empty).
questions.explanation: Ethylene's 2π system has ψ₁ (bonding, in-phase, filled) as HOMO and ψ₂ (antibonding, out-of-phase, vacant) as LUMO.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: How does the greater electronegativity of oxygen alter the frontier molecular orbitals of formaldehyde (H₂C=O)?

options.label: A
options.text: The π HOMO has larger orbital coefficient on oxygen, while the π* LUMO has a larger orbital coefficient on carbon.

options.label: B
options.text: Both carbon and oxygen have identical MO coefficients.

options.label: C
options.text: The π* LUMO is localized 100% on oxygen.

options.label: D
options.text: The π HOMO is localized exclusively on carbon.

questions.correct_answer: The π HOMO has larger orbital coefficient on oxygen, while the π* LUMO has a larger orbital coefficient on carbon.
questions.explanation: Electronegative oxygen lowers orbital energy, polarizing the filled π HOMO toward oxygen and the empty π* LUMO toward electrophilic carbon.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Why do nucleophiles attack carbonyl carbons at an angle of approximately 107° (the Bürgi-Dunitz angle)?

options.label: A
options.text: Because attack at 90° breaks the carbon-carbon single bonds.

options.label: B
options.text: Because nucleophiles only move in hexagonal paths.

options.label: C
options.text: To maximize constructive overlap with the large lobe of the π* LUMO while minimizing electrostatic repulsion from the filled π and nonbonding oxygen electrons.

options.label: D
options.text: Because 107° is the bond angle of water.

questions.correct_answer: To maximize constructive overlap with the large lobe of the π* LUMO while minimizing electrostatic repulsion from the filled π and nonbonding oxygen electrons.
questions.explanation: Attack at ~107° provides optimal overlap with the outward-projecting π* LUMO lobe at the carbonyl carbon.

questions.correct_answer: sp (50% s-character, lowest energy) < sp² (33% s-character) < sp³ (25% s-character, highest energy).
questions.explanation: Greater s-character places electrons closer to the positively charged nucleus, lowering the orbital potential energy.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In Frontier Molecular Orbital theory, what do the acronyms HOMO and LUMO represent?

options.label: A
options.text: Hybrid Orbital Molecular Overlap and Linear Unhybridized Molecular Orbital.

options.label: B
options.text: High Order Magnetic Orbital and Low Order Magnetic Orbital.

options.label: C
options.text: Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO, the electron donor) and Lowest Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (LUMO, the electron acceptor).

options.label: D
options.text: Helical Octet Molecular Octupole and Linear Unpaired Molecular Orbital.

questions.correct_answer: Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO, the electron donor) and Lowest Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (LUMO, the electron acceptor).
questions.explanation: The HOMO acts as the nucleophile/electron donor; the LUMO acts as the electrophile/electron acceptor in chemical reactions.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What orbital interaction forms the ground-state H₂ molecule from two hydrogen 1s atomic orbitals?

options.label: A
options.text: Out-of-phase destructive overlap yielding a σ* orbital.

options.label: B
options.text: Sideways p-orbital overlap.

options.label: C
options.text: Non-bonding electrostatic attraction without orbital mixing.

options.label: D
options.text: In-phase constructive overlap of two 1s atomic orbitals yielding a low-energy σ bonding molecular orbital with zero nodes between nuclei.

questions.correct_answer: In-phase constructive overlap of two 1s atomic orbitals yielding a low-energy σ bonding molecular orbital with zero nodes between nuclei.
questions.explanation: Constructive in-phase overlap of 1s orbitals concentrates electron density between nuclei, lowering the energy to form the σ_1s MO.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: According to Molecular Orbital theory, how are the 8 valence electrons of methane (CH₄) distributed among MOs?

options.label: A
options.text: All 8 electrons are in eight separate, isolated single-bond orbitals.

options.label: B
options.text: Two electrons in a non-degenerate, lowest-energy a₁ MO (from C 2s) and six electrons in three degenerate t₂ MOs (from C 2p).

options.label: C
options.text: Eight electrons in four degenerate non-bonding orbitals.

options.label: D
options.text: All 8 electrons in a single giant spherical orbital.

questions.correct_answer: Two electrons in a non-degenerate, lowest-energy a₁ MO (from C 2s) and six electrons in three degenerate t₂ MOs (from C 2p).
questions.explanation: Photoelectron spectroscopy confirms methane has two discrete valence ionization energies corresponding to a₁ and triply degenerate t₂ MOs.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What are the quantum characteristics of the HOMO and LUMO in neutral ethylene (H₂C=CH₂)?

options.label: A
options.text: The HOMO is the π bonding orbital (ψ₁, zero vertical nodes, 2 electrons); the LUMO is the π* antibonding orbital (ψ₂, one vertical node, empty).

options.label: B
options.text: Both HOMO and LUMO are completely filled with 4 electrons.

options.label: C
options.text: The HOMO is ψ₂ and the LUMO is ψ₁.

options.label: D
options.text: The HOMO has two nodes and the LUMO has zero nodes.

questions.correct_answer: The HOMO is the π bonding orbital (ψ₁, zero vertical nodes, 2 electrons); the LUMO is the π* antibonding orbital (ψ₂, one vertical node, empty).
questions.explanation: Ethylene's 2π system has ψ₁ (bonding, in-phase, filled) as HOMO and ψ₂ (antibonding, out-of-phase, vacant) as LUMO.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: How does the greater electronegativity of oxygen alter the frontier molecular orbitals of formaldehyde (H₂C=O)?

options.label: A
options.text: The π* LUMO is localized 100% on oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: The π HOMO has larger orbital coefficient on oxygen, while the π* LUMO has a larger orbital coefficient on carbon.

options.label: C
options.text: The π HOMO is localized exclusively on carbon.

options.label: D
options.text: Both carbon and oxygen have identical MO coefficients.

questions.correct_answer: The π HOMO has larger orbital coefficient on oxygen, while the π* LUMO has a larger orbital coefficient on carbon.
questions.explanation: Electronegative oxygen lowers orbital energy, polarizing the filled π HOMO toward oxygen and the empty π* LUMO toward electrophilic carbon.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Why do nucleophiles attack carbonyl carbons at an angle of approximately 107° (the Bürgi-Dunitz angle)?

options.label: A
options.text: Because nucleophiles only move in hexagonal paths.

options.label: B
options.text: Because 107° is the bond angle of water.

options.label: C
options.text: Because attack at 90° breaks the carbon-carbon single bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: To maximize constructive overlap with the large lobe of the π* LUMO while minimizing electrostatic repulsion from the filled π and nonbonding oxygen electrons.

questions.correct_answer: To maximize constructive overlap with the large lobe of the π* LUMO while minimizing electrostatic repulsion from the filled π and nonbonding oxygen electrons.
questions.explanation: Attack at ~107° provides optimal overlap with the outward-projecting π* LUMO lobe at the carbonyl carbon.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Atomic Orbital Nodes and Energy Levels
questions.question: How many radial and planar nodes are present in an unhybridized carbon 2p orbital?

options.label: A
options.text: Three perpendicular nodal planes.

options.label: B
options.text: Two spherical nodal surfaces.

options.label: C
options.text: One planar nodal plane passing through the nucleus and zero radial nodes.

options.label: D
options.text: Zero nodes of any kind.

questions.correct_answer: One planar nodal plane passing through the nucleus and zero radial nodes.
questions.explanation: A 2p atomic orbital possesses exactly one planar nodal plane passing through the nucleus where electron density is zero.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Sigma vs Pi Bonding Molecular Orbitals
questions.question: What is the orbital symmetry characteristic of a C-C σ bonding molecular orbital compared to a π orbital?

options.label: A
options.text: The π orbital is spherically symmetric like an s orbital.

options.label: B
options.text: The σ orbital has two perpendicular nodal planes.

options.label: C
options.text: The σ orbital is cylindrically symmetric around the internuclear axis, whereas the π orbital has a nodal plane containing the internuclear axis.

options.label: D
options.text: Both σ and π orbitals have identical symmetry.

questions.correct_answer: The σ orbital is cylindrically symmetric around the internuclear axis, whereas the π orbital has a nodal plane containing the internuclear axis.
questions.explanation: Sigma bonds feature cylindrical symmetry along the bond axis; pi bonds have electron density above and below a central nodal plane.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the spatial topology and nodal structure of a C-C σ* antibonding orbital?

options.label: A
options.text: It has zero nodes between the atoms.

options.label: B
options.text: It has all electron density concentrated directly between the nuclei.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a continuous torus of electron density.

options.label: D
options.text: It possesses a nodal plane perpendicular to the internuclear axis between the two carbon nuclei, with major lobes pointing outward 180° away.

questions.correct_answer: It possesses a nodal plane perpendicular to the internuclear axis between the two carbon nuclei, with major lobes pointing outward 180° away.
questions.explanation: Antibonding σ* orbitals have destructive interference between the nuclei, creating a perpendicular nodal plane and outward-directed lobes.
